title: Understanding the Model
text:
Wesley's model is a linear regression model with transformations applied to the features. The model is given by:

\( \hat{y}_i=\hat{	heta}_0+\hat{	heta}_1(x_{i1})**{3}+\hat{	heta}_{2}\log(x_{i2}) \)

This means that the predictions are based on a linear combination of the transformed features.

title: Linear Combination of Outcomes
text: A linear combination of outcomes means that the predicted values \( \hat{Y} \) can be expressed as a sum of the outcomes \( Y \) multiplied by some coefficients. In this context, the model's predictions are based on the transformed features, not directly on the outcomes \( Y \).

title: Optimal Solution in OLS
text: In Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), the optimal solution refers to the set of parameters \( \hat{\theta}_0, \hat{\theta}_1, \hat{\theta}_2 \) that minimize the sum of squared differences between the observed outcomes \( Y \) and the predicted values \( \hat{Y} \).

title: Checking the Statement
text: Given the model and the definition of a linear combination, does the vector of predictions \( \hat{Y} \) have to be a linear combination of the outcomes \( Y \)?
